title: Launch runway choreography & release-notes conductor for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: orchestrate a deterministic launch runway that coordinates milestone handoffs across API, Console, and Runtime teams, and deliver a single coherent release-notes package and GTM comm-kit.

Scope: cross-team milestones, scope-freeze guardrails, cut criteria (what can be delayed vs must-block), release-notes editorial workflow (content, localization, approvals), embargo windows, support/runbook readiness, and GTM readiness checklist. This ticket is the PM-conductor: align owners, validate signals, and publish final cut decisions.

Success metrics:
- All three component launch notes published and localized by doc-freeze + 72 hours.
- No critical (P0) regressions in canary or preflight; otherwise automated rollback path exercised during staged rollout.
- Customer-facing changelog entry published and distributed to top 20 active customers.
- Post-launch hotfix (<24h) rate < 5% of deployed changes.

Milestones (proposed):
- 2026-02-24: Feature-complete freeze (no new feature merges that affect public API/console surfaces without PM approval).
- 2026-03-01: Integration smoke + canary rollout window (internal + beta customers).
- 2026-03-07: Doc freeze (final release-note drafts due).
- 2026-03-10: Cut decision meeting (scope lock; explicit list of deferred items).
- 2026-03-14: Target public rollout (staged across regions).

Scope-freeze guardrails:
- Any API contract change must have API review, migration notes, and a compatibility flag in runtime; otherwise blocked.
- Console UI surface changes require design sign-off and automated UI regression test coverage.
- Runtime kernel or quantization changes that can affect inference outputs require a quality regression run on the canonical eval set and sign-off from Applied ML.

Cut criteria (must-block vs deferable):
- Must-block if: causes public API contract change without migration, increases error-rate by >1% on production traces in staging, or creates an unrecoverable data path.
- Deferable if: non-blocking perf improvement, docs copy refinements, non-critical telemetry tagging, or UX polish behind a feature-flag.

Release-notes conductor workflow:
- Owners assigned by component: API (PM: Jordan Miles), Console (PM: Priya Singh), Runtime (PM: Diego Marquez). PM-conductor (this ticket) consolidates and edits unified narrative.
- Template: summary, user impact, migration steps, opt-in flags, known issues, roll-back notes, links to support runbook.
- Localization plan: start translation by 2026-03-02 for priority locales (EN, DE, FR, JP). Allow 5 business days.
- Approvals: Engineering lead + Design lead + Security sign-off (if surface-exposed). Final approver: Head of Product (Aisha Patel).

GTM & comms tasks (owner list included):
- Changelog blog + product announcement (Marketing: Carla Huang) - draft due 2026-03-08.
- Customer advisory email targeted to enterprise customers (Sales Ops: Mateo Ruiz) - approval by 2026-03-09.
- Release webinar & demo script (Developer Relations: Nina Park) - rehearsal 2026-03-12.
- Marketplace & partner update pack (Partnerships: Oliver Reed) - prepare artifacts by 2026-03-05.

Support & ops readiness:
- Support runbook with triage flows and KB links (Support: Raghav Iyer) - publish by doc freeze.
- Playbook for rollback and hotfixes, including rollback trigger thresholds and owners.
- Telemetry dashboards to monitor: per-route latency P95, token-cost deviation, error-rate by model, request-fanout counts. Dashboards owner: Observability team (ENG-7124).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Last-minute runtime quantization introduces quality regressions. Mitigation: block deploy until eval pass; maintain immediate fallback model variant for staged traffic.
- Risk: Localization lag delays external release notes. Mitigation: ship English notes and append localized updates in first follow-up.

Artifacts and links: see artifacts field for document locations and PRs.

Notes: This ticket is intentionally prescriptive — it includes gating criteria and a single PM-conductor rhythm (twice-weekly 30-minute standups during runway) to reduce ad-hoc decision-making.
